req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid URL
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter of /redirect-to is missing or malformed.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must return HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter is missing or malformed. Examining the source code (lines 572-644), the handler does `response.headers['Location'] = args['url'].encode('utf-8')` with no guard — if 'url' is absent, a KeyError is raised (which Flask converts to 500, not 400). This means the current implementation does NOT satisfy R-HTTPBIN-027 for the missing-url case. Tests must be written to assert the REQUIRED behavior (400) so they will FAIL on the current (buggy) implementation and PASS only when the requirement is correctly implemented. This maximises mutation kill rate by asserting exact status codes. We cover: (1) positive — valid url yields 302 redirect, (2) negative — missing url yields 400, (3) negative — malformed/empty url yields 400, (4) boundary — url param present but empty string yields 400, (5) decision-table — status_code override with missing url still yields 400.

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_url_with_custom_status_code_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
